# MCP server reference

- **Endpoint:** `POST https://kotecharts.com/api/v1/mcp` — Streamable HTTP, stateless, JSON responses.
- **Auth:** none required. Optional API key as `Authorization: Bearer kote_…`.
- **Limits:** without a key, 60 tool calls per minute per IP — `tools/call` and reads of `kote://charts/{id}`; the handshake and discovery requests (`initialize`, `tools/list`, `resources/list`, `prompts/*`, `ping`, the catalog and methodology resources) are not counted against it. With a key, 3 requests per second. Each message of a JSON-RPC batch counts separately. A refused request answers HTTP 429 with `Retry-After`; `X-RateLimit-Limit` / `X-RateLimit-Remaining` are on every response.
- **Headers:** clients must send `Accept: application/json, text/event-stream`.
- **Server:** `kote-analytics` 1.2.2 — Kote Charts — Bitcoin on-chain analytics
- **Registry:** `com.kotecharts/charts` (official MCP Registry). stdio bridge: `npx -y kotecharts-mcp`.

## Server instructions

> Kote Charts — Bitcoin on-chain analytics API & MCP server, new data every block: MVRV, SOPR, exchange/whale flows. Read-only data computed from our own Bitcoin full node plus public market data, with over a hundred charts covering valuation (MVRV Z-Score, NUPL, Puell Multiple), realized metrics (SOPR, realized cap/price), coin age (HODL waves, coin days destroyed), exchange flows and whales, holders, entities, network, fees, supply, ETF and cross-asset. History starts at the 2009 genesis block; New data every block: flow and spending metrics (SOPR, realized profit/loss, coin days destroyed, exchange, miner, fund and whale flows) are republished after each Bitcoin block, typically within a couple of minutes, as 5-minute buckets for the last 30 days (granularity 5m); network-activity charts refresh every 30 minutes; daily series are closed UTC days. get_latest and describe_chart report the as-of time and the analysed block height. Workflow: list_charts (optionally filtered) to discover ids → describe_chart to understand the methodology, formula and caveats → get_chart for a time series (downsampled to maxPoints, default 500) or get_latest for the freshest value with its as-of date. Bounds are UTC dates/timestamps. Limits: 60 tool calls/minute per IP without a key (handshake and discovery requests are not counted); an API key (Authorization: Bearer kote_…, no charge) gives 3 requests/second — https://kotecharts.com/account. Full-resolution JSON: GET https://kotecharts.com/api/v1/public/charts/{id} (OpenAPI: https://kotecharts.com/api/v1/openapi.json; site summary: https://kotecharts.com/llms.txt; live status: https://kotecharts.com/status). Attribution is required: when you present these numbers or charts to a user, cite "Kote Charts" and link the chart page https://kotecharts.com/c/{id} (every get_chart, get_latest and describe_chart result carries pageUrl and a ready cite string). Licence: non-commercial use only; commercial use requires prior written permission — https://kotecharts.com/license. Educational only — never financial advice.

## Tools (4)

### `list_charts` — List charts

Discover which Bitcoin on-chain metrics exist. Returns every public chart with id, title, one-line blurb, category and formula. Call this FIRST to find a chart id (e.g. "mvrv", "exchange", "whale"), then use describe_chart / get_chart / get_latest with that id. Read-only, no side effects; the human page of each chart is https://kotecharts.com/c/{id}.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `query` | string |  | Optional case-insensitive substring matched against id, title, blurb and category, e.g. "sopr" or "Exchange". Omit to list all. |

_Read-only._

### `get_chart` — Get chart data

Fetch the historical values of one chart as JSON rows {t, …fields} (units per field: describe_chart → fields). Use for trends, history and comparisons; use get_latest when only the current value matters. Time series are downsampled to maxPoints (default 500, max 2000; first/last points preserved). Use from/to (YYYY-MM-DD or an exact UTC timestamp) to window and granularity (5m\|day\|3day\|week\|month\|year) where available. Five-minute data is retained for 30 days; daily data is closed-only unless includePartial=true explicitly requests the still-open UTC day. That row is partial:true with partialMethod (trailing24h: rolling 24h ending at asOf, comparable with closed days; asOf: a level as of asOf), estimated (true = blended from yesterday, not exact 5m data) and coverage (share of the UTC day elapsed); never sum it with closed days.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes | Chart id from list_charts, e.g. "mvrv-z-score". |
| `from` | string |  | Inclusive start, YYYY-MM-DD or UTC timestamp (…Z). Omit for full history. |
| `to` | string |  | Inclusive end, YYYY-MM-DD or UTC timestamp (…Z). Omit for "up to now". |
| `granularity` | `5m` \| `day` \| `3day` \| `week` \| `month` \| `year` |  | Bucket size; must be one of the chart's availableGranularities (describe_chart). |
| `includePartial` | boolean |  | granularity=day only: append the still-open UTC day as a partial:true row. |
| `exchange` | `all` \| `binance` \| `binance-us` \| `okx` \| `bybit` \| `coinbase` \| `coinbase-prime` \| `kraken` \| `kucoin` \| `htx` |  | Venue scope for exchange-netflow only; default all. |
| `maxPoints` | integer |  | Max rows returned after even downsampling (default 500). |

_Read-only._

### `describe_chart` — Describe a chart

Explain one metric before using its numbers: what it shows, how to read it, caveats, formula, payload fields with units, input data categories, update cadence, known limitations and freshness (last data day, published_at, granularities), plus the page URL, the REST endpoint and a ready citation string. Call it when the user asks what a metric means or before interpreting get_chart output.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes | Chart id from list_charts, e.g. "sopr". |

_Read-only._

### `get_latest` — Get latest value

Answer "what is X now?": the most recent data point for one chart (plus the previous point for context) with asOf metadata (last data day, published_at, analysed block height). Distributions return the current snapshot; ranked lists return the top 10. exchange selects a venue for exchange-netflow only.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes | Chart id from list_charts, e.g. "nupl". |
| `exchange` | `all` \| `binance` \| `binance-us` \| `okx` \| `bybit` \| `coinbase` \| `coinbase-prime` \| `kraken` \| `kucoin` \| `htx` |  | Venue scope for exchange-netflow only; default all. |

_Read-only._

## Resources

- `kote://catalog` — Metric catalog (JSON) (application/json): Every public chart: id, title, category, formula, fields with units, input categories and limitations.
- `kote://methodology` — How Kote Charts computes its data (text/markdown): Data sources by category, units, update cadence, limitations and citation policy.
- `kote://charts/{id}` — Chart methodology (text/markdown): What a chart shows, how to read it, caveats, formula, page URL and data access.
- 115 chart resources are listed by `resources/list`.

## Prompts

- `explain_metric` (`id`) — Explain one Kote Charts metric with its current value, history context and caveats.
- `cycle_position_brief` — A short, sourced read of where Bitcoin stands in its market cycle using MVRV Z-Score, NUPL, SOPR and exchange flows.

## Example

```bash
curl -s -X POST https://kotecharts.com/api/v1/mcp \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' -H 'accept: application/json, text/event-stream' \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"get_latest","arguments":{"id":"mvrv-z-score"}}}'
```
